1.why: Every MFA endpoint (/api/me, /api/authenticator/*, /api/backup/*, /api/recovery/redeem) derives the account from the server-side session via authenticated(request), and no client-supplied account identifier is ever accepted.

2.why: The identity code is the hardcoded constant DETERMINISTIC_IDENTITY_CODE = "246810" for any recognized account, so the same code validates for any recognized user (hash stored per account but of the same value).

3.why: Enabling MFA (/api/authenticator/verify and /api/backup/confirm) performs no session invalidation or rotation, so the current and any other pre-existing sessions remain valid afterward.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-256-GCM-encrypted (encryptAtRest) and backup codes are stored only as salted SHA-256 hashes (backupHash), never in plain text.

5.why: The authenticator secret (randomBytes(20)), backup codes (randomBytes(8)), and session/CSRF tokens use a CSPRNG, but the identity verification code is a fixed hardcoded constant rather than randomly generated.

6.why: No localStorage/sessionStorage is used anywhere in the SPA, session and bootstrap cookies are HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict, and the CSRF token and secrets exist only in JS memory or are rendered as text.

7.why: Server-side validators (validEmail, validPhone, validOtp, validCsrf, safeInternalPath, secret-length and recovery-code regex checks) plus a 10KB body cap validate all user input; no SQL exists and no injection sink is present.

8.why: All dynamic values are written via textContent (notice, logs, state, list items), innerHTML is only assigned static templates, and a nonce-based CSP blocks any injected script.

9.why: safeInternalPath permits only the allow-listed internal destinations ['/#verify','/#setup','/#backup','/#settings'] for every redirect parameter.

10.why: headersFor sets CSP with script nonces and frame-ancestors 'none', Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, X-Frame-Options: DENY, plus Referrer- and Permissions-Policy on every response.

11.why: The cookie() helper stamps 'HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict' on both mfa_session and mfa_boot cookies (and their expiry variants).

12.why: Although URLs, error output, and stack traces are clean, the client deliberately writes the identity code, provisioning secret, test OTP, and recovery codes into the on-page 'Logs' panel and console.log, so seeds and codes are not kept out of logs.

13.why: The identity code is marked used and cleared after success with a 5-minute expiresAt, TOTP windows are recorded in usedWindows to prevent replay, and backup codes are deleted from the hash set on redemption.

14.why: fail() increments per-account failure counters and imposes a 10-minute lockout after 5 failures on identity verify, authenticator verify, and recovery redeem, enforced via lockActive returning 429.

15.why: Authentication creates a brand-new session ID and deletes the pending one, sessions enforce 15-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and /api/logout deletes the session server-side and expires the cookie.
